title: Housing progress report and two development applications
subtitle: Heritage designations, 70 Fountain Street tower, Victoria Road lands, brownfield incentives, and a withdrawn provincial letter motion.
overview: Council received the Housing in Guelph 2025 report {{vote:m6}}. Staff described rising housing units in development applications, lower building permit numbers, and work on grants, servicing and affordable housing. Council also directed staff to explore re-establishing the Brownfield Community Improvement Plan and report back in early 2027 {{vote:m8}}.

Two statutory public meetings were held. Council received reports on a proposed 24-storey rental building at 70 Fountain Street East {{vote:m4}} and on land use and zoning changes for the 328 Victoria Road South and 588 Stone Road East lands {{vote:m5}}. Receiving a report is not a decision on the application, and staff will return with recommendations later.

Council also authorized notices of intention to designate 225 Waterloo Avenue {{vote:m2}} and 35 Foster Avenue {{vote:m3}} under the Ontario Heritage Act. A councillor's proposed letter asking the province for a two-year pause on Planning Act changes was withdrawn before a vote. A closed session was an education session on land use planning and legal matters, and no decisions were made.

decisions.detail: Council authorized the Clerk to publish and serve notice of intention to designate 225 Waterloo Avenue, with the by-law returning if no objections arrive within thirty days {{vote:m2}}.
Council authorized notice of intention to designate 35 Foster Avenue under the Ontario Heritage Act, with the by-law returning if no objections are received {{vote:m3}}.
Council received the statutory public meeting report on applications for a 24-storey mixed-use building with 419 rental units, retail space and five stacked townhouses {{vote:m4}}.

decisions.item: 328 Victoria Road South and 588 Stone Road East
decisions.detail: Council received the statutory public meeting report on Official Plan and zoning amendments to support subdivision of the lands {{vote:m5}}.
Council received the annual housing report summarizing progress on housing units, infrastructure, grants and affordable housing work {{vote:m6}}.
Staff were directed to explore next steps to re-establish the plan and report back to Council in early 2027 {{vote:m8}}.

debate: On 70 Fountain Street East, a nearby resident supported more people downtown but asked that parking exits be moved from Farquhar Street to Fountain Street, citing poor visibility and difficult turns. Staff said they would consider this during traffic review.

Several councillors raised parking and height. Concerns included tenants parking on nearby streets with fewer spaces than units, and measuring building height from the Farquhar Street grade instead of the lower grade. One councillor asked for ground-level renderings. The applicant said student demand for parking is lower and parking is sized with its transportation engineer.

Councillors asked whether the building would serve families, not only students. The applicant said about a third of units are two or three bedrooms, with larger three-bedroom units, and that the building is open to anyone. One councillor noted that planning rules cannot regulate who lives in a building.
Downtown speakers and councillors worried that overlapping construction and staging could hurt existing businesses, and asked that the on-street parking review consider these developments.

A trail users' delegate supported the Victoria Road and Stone Road application, praising its trail connections and a land use agreement with a hiking club. The delegate raised separate concerns about rail siding activity affecting trails.

On the proposed provincial moratorium letter, supporters cited staff time spent responding to legislative changes. Others said the wording was too broad, could oppose helpful legislation, and was not well scoped. The mover withdrew it to bring back a more defined version.
